TestLWTPaxos::test_paxos_grace_seconds_b.description: 3-node RF=3 cluster in 3 racks (auth with tablets for $paxos access), one session with host-pinned reads (session.execute(host=)). Creates a table with paxos_grace_seconds=cql_timeout(3) and one with default; LWT-inserts one key into the default table and asserts its paxos state on a quorum, then LWT-inserts at CL=ALL into the short table with a quorum-presence check (retried with a new key if the check outlasted the grace window, SCYLLADB-5753). TestPaxosBug::test_synced_most_recent_co.description: Regression for CASSANDRA-12043 (expired most-recent-commit causing endless paxos repair / CAS timeouts). 3 nodes in 3 racks, RF=3, table with paxos_grace_seconds=40 (80 in debug). Node C stopped, LWT INSERT IF NOT EXISTS at QUORUM on A+B (t0); B stopped and C started (asserted to take < grace-10s), SERIAL read via A at t0+grace/2 (A+C quorum, C missing MRC -> paxos repair replays it to C with a fresh TTL); second SERIAL read at t0+grace+5 (A's MRC expired, C's alive; asserts read 1 didn't overrun) must not time out. Only asserts no exception; returned row not checked.

TestPaxosBug::test_synced_most_recent_co.relevance: Live: scylla implements the CASSANDRA-12043 mitigation since initial LWT (b3e01a45d7, d1774693bf): service/paxos/prepare_summary.cc:30-45 replicas_missing_most_recent_commit ignores MRC older than paxos_grace_seconds; service/paxos/paxos_state.cc:142 uses ballot time as 'now' when loading state. Paxos state TTL = paxos_grace_seconds relative to write time (paxos_state.cc:324-328, 'USING TIMESTAMP ? AND TTL ?'), so C's replayed MRC outlives A's.
